title: What shape do all the points at one distance from P make?
description: The video imagines every point that is four centimetres from P, not just a few. It joins each point to P with a line of the same length and sees what shape the ends make. Keeko raises the doubt that the points would make a straight line.
teaching_notes: One idea: all points at one fixed distance from P make a circle around P. Watch for children who picture only left and right, and so think the points fall on a straight line.

source: Imagine marking all the points of 4 cm distance from the point P. How would they look?
video_script.why: The child pictures every point at one distance from P and sees that they make a round shape, not a line.
video_script.substitution: Join P to each point with a four centimetre line and watch where the ends fall.
video_script.anchor: A point P with four centimetre lines going out from it in many directions
video_script.wrong_answer: they would make a straight line
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko pictures only the points to the left and the right of P, so the points seem to lie on a straight line. A point above P is also four centimetres away and is not on that line.
video_script.payoff_line: They make a circle, with P in the middle.

final_answer.value: a circle around P, every point 4 cm from P
final_answer.spoken: they make a circle with P in the middle, and every point of it is four centimetres from P

maths_rules: Every joining line from P to a point is 4 cm long.
Points in every direction at 4 cm from P make a round curve around P.
Two points on opposite sides of P are 4 cm + 4 cm = 8 cm apart.
video_script.design: One idea: all points at one distance from P form a circle. Assumes the child has marked some points with a ruler. Wrong idea: the points lie on a line. P stays all video.

Not a few points only, but all of them.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How would they look?

<bookmark mark='same'/>If each point is four centimetres from P, the lines joining them to P are all equally long.

Join it to P, and the line is four centimetres long.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: points in every direction; joined, they give a round curve around P

narration: <bookmark mark='every'/>Step three, do this in every direction.
The ends of the lines never come closer to P and never go further from it.
<bookmark mark='join'/>Joining all the points gives a perfectly round curve.

beats.on_screen: Answer: a circle around P, every point 4 cm from P
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>They make a circle, with P in the middle.
Every point of it is four centimetres from P.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a straight line through P with two dots, one on each side; a new dot four centimetres above P sits off the line; the bubble is struck out in the warning colour

marks.doubt: a bubble shows a straight line through P with a dot on each side
marks.fix: a dot four centimetres above P appears off the line
marks.strike: the bubble is struck out and the round curve is drawn

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks they would make a straight line, with P in the middle.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But a point four centimetres above P is also in the picture.
It is not on that straight line.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>Points in every direction curve round P.
